facts.fact_text: The applicant, Genderdoc-M, is a non-governmental organisation based in Moldova.
The applicant, Genderdoc-M, has as its object to provide information and to assist the LGBT community.
On 7 April 2005, the applicant association applied to Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful demonstration.
The peaceful demonstration for which the applicant association sought authorisation was to be held in front of the Parliament on 27 May 2005.
The purpose of the proposed demonstration was to encourage the adoption of laws to protect sexual minorities from discrimination.
On 27 April 2005, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected the applicant association's application to hold a demonstration.
On 6 May 2005, the Chişinău Mayor's Office refused permission for the proposed demonstration.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 5 that assemblies may be held only after the organisers have duly notified the urban mayor's (municipal) or rural offices.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 11(1) that the organiser of an assembly must lodge a notification with the mayor's office at least fifteen days before the chosen date, according to the model provided in the appendix to that law.

Law no. 560-XIII of 21 July 1995 regarding the organisation and conduct of assemblies provides under Section 13 that after examining the preliminary declaration, the Mayor's Office shall issue one of the following decisions and inform the organiser: grant permission, or refuse permission under section 12(6).

Section 34 of Law no. 123 of 18 March 2003 regarding local public administration provides that the Mayor undertakes measures forbidding or suspending shows, presentations and other public demonstrations which contradict legal order and morals.

Article 54(1) of the Moldovan Constitution provides that the exercise of certain rights or freedoms may be restricted only under the law and only as required for: the defence of national security, of public order, health or morals, of citizens' rights and freedoms, the carrying out of investigations in criminal cases, the prevention of the consequences of a natural calamity or of a technological disaster.

The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the arguments relied on by the Chişinău Mayor's Office to justify its refusal to authorise the assembly were legally ungrounded, as the law does not provide such grounds for the non-authorisation of an assembly.

The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the decision as to whether to authorise or not to authorise an assembly should not be made conditional on the nature of the problems the participants intend to bring to society's attention.
The Chişinău Court of Appeal found that the decision as to whether to authorise or not to authorise an assembly should not be made conditional on the status of those problems.
On 14 June 2006, the Chişinău Court of Appeal found against the applicant association on re-examination.
